author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Trump administration is escalating economic pressure on Iran, targeting foreign banks, companies and intermediaries accused of helping Tehran generate revenue. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the “Operation Economic Outcast” campaign will target the networks supporting Iranian oil exports and could eventually cut non-compliant businesses off from the US financial system. The Treasury has sanctioned nearly 60 entities and expanded the threat of secondary sanctions to shipping, aviation, gold, technology and digital assets. China, Iran’s largest oil buyer, is likely to face particular scrutiny as Tehran continues using middlemen, foreign banks and a shadow fleet to circumvent sanctions. Bessent says countries and companies have been given a chance to change course, but warned those that do not comply could “leave the dollar system”. 

Al Jazeera’s Eva McKend reports from Washington, DC.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The US State Department has removed Syria from its list of "State Sponsors of Terrorism", ending nearly five decades of isolation. In an interview with Al Jazeera, former US Special Envoy for Syria Michael Ratney said the decision was "the right one" and necessary to let the Syrian economy "breathe". He said the designation made sense under Bashar al-Assad but "makes much less sense" under Ahmad al-Sharaa. Ratney said the move gives businesses "clarity and faith that they can engage in Syria without legal liability", which should have "knock-on effects for Syrians". He said al-Sharaa's ideology is "deeply antithetical to the Iranians" and that it "doesn't surprise me at all" that one of his first steps was to cut Iran's access to Hezbollah. Addressing Syria-Israel talks, Ratney said the decision strengthens al-Sharaa's hand by showing "the US is on his side", while criticising Israel for continuing to "stoke instability" in Syria.

title: Removing sanctions gives Syria's economy a chance to breathe: Analysis
